title: Local lifting criterion for ideal-fraction and saturated log charts
statement:
Let $U=(\operatorname{Spec}A,N)$ be the fine log scheme associated to a chart $\alpha:P\to A$ by a finitely generated integral monoid $P$ [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, def-trf-fine-log-etale-descent-datum]. Let $E\subset P$ be finite and nonempty and let $\mathcal I\subset N$ be the log ideal generated by its images. Write $G=P^{\mathrm{gp}}$, $Q_e=\langle P,h-e\ (h\in E)\rangle\subset G$ and $Q_e^s=\{q\in G:\exists n>0,\ nq\in Q_e\}$. For $R=Q_e$ or $Q_e^s$ equip
$$C_R=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[R])$$
with its associated chart log structure and its natural map to $U$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Let $g:(T,M_T)\to U$ be any fine log morphism and $e\in E$. There is a log morphism $(T,M_T)\to C_{Q_e}$ over $U$ if and only if, at every geometric stalk, every $g(h)$ with $h\in E$ belongs to $g(e)+M_T$; when it exists it is unique. Its chart map sends $h-e$ to the unique difference $g(h)-g(e)$ in $M_T^{\mathrm{gp}}$. If $T$ is fs, the identical criterion gives a unique lift to $C_{Q_e^s}$, extending this group map. No Noetherian assumption on $T$ is made.
If $g^*\mathcal I$ is locally principal, $T$ admits a strict etale cover on each member of which some $g(e)$ generates it and the indicated lifts exist. On a locus where both $g(e)$ and $g(f)$ generate, the difference $g(f)-g(e)$ is a unit; the two lifts factor through the respective principal opens $D(z^{f-e})$ and $D(z^{e-f})$ and agree under their common-localization isomorphism, for both kinds of charts. Conversely a lift to either kind of chart makes the pulled-back ideal generated by its distinguished $e$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.19 and 3.1.21, printed p. 101; 3.3.6(ii), 3.3.8--3.3.9, printed pp. 107--108: universal chart lifting and saturation.

proof.text: Write $m_p=g(p)\in\Gamma(T,M_T)$ and use additive notation for monoids (the structural map still takes sums to products of functions). A chart at a geometric point $t$ expresses $M_{T,t}$ as $P_t\oplus_{F_t}\mathcal O_{T,t}^{\times}$ with integral $P_t$. The integral unit-pushout lemma gives cancellation, without any injectivity assumption on $F_t\to\mathcal O_{T,t}^{\times}$. Equalities of germs spread to pointed etale neighbourhoods: use the small-site convention, the cofilteredness of pointed neighbourhoods, and the elementwise equality criterion for filtered colimits. Consequently the assumed divisibilities give, locally at every $t$, sections $b_h$ with $m_e+b_h=m_h$. Since $E$ is finite we choose one common neighbourhood for these finitely many equations. Cancellation makes each $b_h$ unique wherever defined, so the sections agree on overlaps and glue by the sheaf axiom. Cancellation also holds for sections: any equality between sections holds at every stalk, and stalkwise cancellation followed by this same germ-and-sheaf argument cancels it globally.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8, principal ideals in integral monoids; 3.1.19 and 3.3.6(ii), expanded by the germ-and-cancellation argument.

proof.text: The homomorphism $p\mapsto m_p$ extends to a group homomorphism $\phi:G\to\Gamma(T,M_T)^{\mathrm{gp}}$: send a formal difference $p-p'$ to $m_p-m_{p'}$; the group-completion relations preserve this formula. Its value at $h-e$ is $b_h$, since $m_e+b_h=m_h$. Hence $\phi(Q_e)$ lies in the embedded submonoid $\Gamma(T,M_T)$: $Q_e$ is generated by $P$ and these differences. Restriction gives a monoid map $v_e:Q_e\to\Gamma(T,M_T)$. Every extension of the given map on $P$ must satisfy $v_e(h-e)+m_e=m_h$, so cancellation fixes its values on every generator and makes it equal to $v_e$. This proves the monoid part of existence and uniqueness, without dividing regular functions or assuming that $\alpha(m_e)$ is a nonzerodivisor.

source.place: VIII 3.1.19, the fraction chart P[a^{-1}I]; 3.3.8, cancellation in an integral monoid.

proof.text:
The map $v_e$ determines the scheme map locally on any affine open $W\subset T$: define
$$a\otimes z^q\longmapsto g^\sharp(a)|_W\,\alpha_T(v_e(q)|_W).$$
The formula is additive on the monoid-ring basis and balanced over $\mathbf Z[P]$, because $\alpha_T(m_p)=g^\sharp(\alpha(p))$; it preserves products since $v_e(q+q')=v_e(q)+v_e(q')$. Thus the tensor universal property gives a ring homomorphism, and the affine-spectrum correspondence gives $W\to C_{Q_e}$. The maps agree on affine subopens by the displayed formula, hence agree on intersections by an affine open cover; scheme-morphism gluing gives $T\to C_{Q_e}$. Apply the arbitrary-scheme chart-logification mapping bijection to $Q_e$ and this scheme map to obtain its unique compatible log map with chart map $v_e$. Its composite to $U$ equals $g$ by the same mapping bijection for $P$. Conversely any log lift has a chart map $w$, with $m_h=m_e+w(h-e)$; thus it implies the stalk criterion. Cancellation fixes $w=v_e$, which fixes the scheme map on affine opens and then the entire log map. This proves the fine criterion and uniqueness.

source.place: VIII 3.3.3 and 3.3.6(ii), printed pp.106--107, expanded into the actual tensor-ring and associated-log maps.

proof.text:
For the fs case we first check saturation of $M_{T,t}$, rather than infer it from a Noetherian hypothesis. Take an fs chart $S$ at $t$, put $F=\alpha^{-1}(\mathcal O_{T,t}^{\times})$, $K=\mathcal O_{T,t}^{\times}$, and write $L=S\oplus_FK$. The integral unit-pushout lemma shows that $L$ is integral, so $L$ embeds in its group completion. In additive notation that group completion is
$$H=(S^{\mathrm{gp}}\oplus K)/\{(z,-f^{\mathrm{gp}}(z)):z\in F^{\mathrm{gp}}\}.$$
Indeed, the images of $S$ and $K$ generate $H$, and its quotient relations are precisely the group versions of the pushout relations. If $nx=[p,k]$ with $p\in S$ and $x=[a,u]\in H$, equality in this quotient gives $na-p=e_1-e_2$ for some $e_1,e_2\in F$. Then
$$n(a+e_2)=p+e_1+(n-1)e_2\in S,$$
so $a+e_2\in S$ by saturation of $S$. Finally $x=[a+e_2,u-f(e_2)]\in L$. This proves saturation of the geometric log stalk, including torsion in the group completion and noninjective $f$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.17 and 3.3.9; elementary verification of saturation in the chart-stalk pushout group presentation.

proof.text: Let $q\in Q_e^s$, so $nq\in Q_e$ for some $n>0$. The stalkwise group extension of $\phi$ has $n\phi_t(q)=v_e(nq)_t\in M_{T,t}$; Step 4 puts $\phi_t(q)$ in $M_{T,t}$. To obtain a section, write $q=p-p'$ with $p,p'\in P$ and use local representatives of the equality $m_{p'}+c=m_p$ at each stalk, exactly as in Step 1. Cancellation glues them uniquely. Therefore the same group map restricts to $v_e^s:Q_e^s\to\Gamma(T,M_T)$, with all additive relations checked in the group completion. The atlas lemma supplies that $Q_e^s$ is finitely generated and integral. Step 3, with $Q_e^s$ in place of $Q_e$, therefore constructs the unique saturated-chart log lift. Any such lift restricts to the fine chart and hence implies the same criterion; uniqueness follows because every element of $Q_e^s\subset G$ is a difference of elements of $P$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.21 and 3.3.9, universal property for saturated test log schemes; 3.3.6(ii), chart realization.

proof.text: Suppose $g^*\mathcal I$ is locally generated by a section $m$. Locally $m$ belongs to the ideal generated by the finite set $\{m_h:h\in E\}$, so at any geometric point it is $m_e+b$ for some $e\in E$, and this equality holds after etale shrinking. Since $m$ generates, after further shrinking $m_e=m+a$ and, for each $h\in E$, $m_h=m+c_h$. The two first equations give $m=m+(a+b)$, so cancellation gives $a+b=0$. Hence $a,b$ are units and $m_e$ itself generates: explicitly $m_h=m_e+(b+c_h)$. Finiteness of $E$ permits all these equations on one neighbourhood. These neighbourhoods form a strict etale cover when endowed with the restricted log structure. Steps 1--3 give the required lifts there, and Step 5 gives their saturated versions when $T$ is fs.

source.place: VIII 3.3.7--3.3.8, coherent ideals and local principality; 3.3.4(ii), strict etale chart restriction.

proof.text: On a member where both $m_e$ and $m_f$ generate, write $m_f=m_e+b$ and $m_e=m_f+c$. Cancellation gives $b+c=0$, so $b=m_f-m_e$ is a unit of the log sheaf. The log axiom identifies $\alpha_T(b)$ with a unit regular function. Under the $e$-lift the function $1\otimes z^{f-e}$ pulls back to $\alpha_T(b)$, and under the $f$-lift $1\otimes z^{e-f}$ pulls back to its inverse. The basic-open pullback lemma therefore puts these maps in the respective principal opens; by the definition of an open subscheme the factorizations are unique, with the restricted log maps. The affine-atlas lemma identifies these two opens by their common localization, also in the saturated case. Under that identification both chart maps are restrictions of the same group map $\phi$: they send $p$ to $m_p$, $f-e$ to $b$, and its inverse to $-b$. The ring formula of Step 3 and the logification bijection then show that the two log morphisms agree.

source.place: VIII 3.1.19 and 3.3.8--3.3.9, overlaps of generator charts and their saturated versions.

proof.text: Finally, on either chart every $h\in E$ satisfies $h=e+(h-e)$ with $h-e\in Q_e\subset Q_e^s$. Pulling this equality back under a log lift makes every $m_h$ belong to $m_e+M_T$. Since $e\in E$, the generated ideal both contains $m_e$ and is contained in its principal ideal; it is exactly $m_e+M_T$. This proves the converse principality assertion, with no condition on the functions $\alpha(e)$ and no finiteness or Noetherian assumption on the test scheme.

source.place: VIII 3.1.19; 3.3.8--3.3.9, the ideal is principal on a distinguished-generator chart.

proof_origin.place: Expansion of VIII 3.1.19--3.1.21 and 3.3.3--3.3.9; explicit cancellation, tensor-ring, saturation and overlap calculations. No SGA source.

The live lem-sfb-integral-monoid-unit-pushout (Q94 port) has the same hypotheses (integral P, a submonoid, a hom to an abelian group with no injectivity) and gives integrality, cancellation and the equality criterion. It lacks only the per twin's explicit-H clause, and Step 4 already proves that H is the group completion of the pushout. FIX: per→sfb in Steps 1/4, proof_deps and tool_uses. Step 4 is reworded so the lemma gives integrality of L and the step gives L^gp=H. The corrected closure is 452 nodes, none dropped, with no cycle. Step checks: (1) stalk divisibility → local b_h via the cofiltered-neighbourhood and filtered-colimit nodes, made unique by cancellation, glued by the sheaf axiom; (2) phi on G, phi(h-e)=b_h; (3) the tensor ring map is balanced since alpha_T(m_p)=g^#alpha(p); affine-spectrum plus scheme-morphism-gluing give the scheme map, and the arbitrary-scheme sfb logification bijection gives the log map, so no Noetherian hypothesis is needed; (4) saturation: n(a+e2)=p+e1+(n-1)e2 in S, and x=[a+e2,u-f(e2)], signs checked; (5) saturation gives Q_e^s sections, and the atlas node supplies fg and integral; (6) a+b=0 by cancellation, so m_e generates; (7) the unit b and the basic-open pullback node place each lift in its D(z^{±(f-e)}), the atlas identity identifies the opens, and phi gives agreement; (8) the converse via h=e+(h-e). Edge cases checked: P=N with E={0,1} (Q_1=Z gives A[1/x], and the criterion is that m_1 is a unit), the N^2 blowup charts, empty T, |E|=1, torsion, alpha(e)=0, non-Noetherian T.
